newsitem.title: USA: Court upholds consolidating breast implant cases.
newsitem.headline: Court upholds consolidating breast implant cases.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co said Thursday that a U.S. Appeals Court has upheld a ruling that would consolidate in federal court tens of thousands of breast implant cases filed against Dow Corning Corp.
The ruling by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit applies to 14,000 cases involving Dow Chemical, which owns 50 percent of Dow Corning, said Dow Chemical spokesman Bob Charlton.
Charlton said it also applies to separate cases involving Corning Inc, which also owns 50 percent of Dow Corning.
The ruling sends the cases, many of which have been languishing in state courts, to the U.S. District Court of the Eastern District of Michigan, Charlton said.
The cases were filed by women claiming silicone gel breast implants from Dow Corning, once the world's largest maker of breast implants, led to health problems.
Many cases have been pending since July of 1996, when Dow Corning entered Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.
"Dow Chemical is arguing that resolution of these in federal court should be resolved during the Dow Corning bankruptcy process," Charlton said.
Dow Chemical said in a statement that the ruling means resolution of the claims will be a part of Dow Corning's bankruptcy resolution process.
Charlton said Dow Corning has already proposed in bankruptcy court a plan of reorganization that includes addressing the claims of these women.
